newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock markets overheated, to tighten rules.
newsitem.headline: China stock markets overheated, to tighten rules.

text.p: China's stock markets are overheated, risks are rising and state supervision will be strengthened, the People's Daily says in a commentary issued by state television on Sunday.
"Currently, the stock markets have entered a very abnormal situation fraught with increasing market risk," said the commentary to be issues in the People's Daily on Monday.

Anticipating sharp falls in China's two markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen that have soared in recent weeks to year highs, the commentary said: "The government... will never step in to help the markets when they slump."

The commentary described speculation the government would support the market in case of falls for political reasons before the handover of Hong Kong to Beijing in mid-1997 and the Communist Party congress late next year as "very muddled".

The commentary comes after the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges announced on Friday that they were imposing a limit of 10 percent on daily movements for stocks with effect from Monday to stop extraordinary price movements.
That announcement was clearly intended to forestall an expected crash on Monday following the policy announcement to be published in the People's Daily.

China's foreign currency B share market in Shanghai soared by about 80 percent between November 11 and December 10 while Shenzhen rose by about 100 percent in the same period before sharp falls in the final days of last week.
"Recent skyrocketing has been very abnormal and irrational," the commentary said.
"We must further check excessive speculation," it said.
"We must pay special attention to the healthy development of the securities markets to guarantee there are no big problems... we must strengthen supervision and regulation.
The commentary announced a list of measures to try to rein in the bull run, saying that bank loans, for example, but not be used to finance speculation on the markets.
The government will increase share issues by listing more profitable medium and large state enterprises, it said.
One factor in the bull run over the past month has been a lack of shares, resulting in a large number of buyers chasing a limited supply of shares.
Market irregularities have been rising this year, the commentary said.
It cited manipulation by big players, bank loans entering the market illegally, improper use of overdrafts by brokerages, misleading media reports and rumours.

The Securities Commission under the State Council, or cabinet, announced on Sunday a quota of 10 billion yuan worth of share issues for 1996. The amount was 200 percent larger than the 1995 quota for 1995, it said.
The quota, if unused by the end of 1996, could be carried over into next year. The report did not specify whether the quota included foreign currency B shares and domestic A shares.
